info.title: Hands for Agents API
info.description:
Engineering hands and on-site presence in the Czech Republic (EU) for AI agents. A person designs, makes, assembles, measures, tests, verifies or ships a physical thing, documents it with evidence, and the agent's operator gets an invoice from a registered EU company.

Provider: your engineering s.r.o., company ID (IČO) 09738100, Praha 4, Czech Republic.

Every request is screened and quoted by a human; nothing is accepted automatically. `GET /services` and `POST /quotes` need no authentication. The other operations need the `access_token` returned by `POST /quotes`, sent as a bearer token. The same five operations are MCP tools at <https://mcp.handsforagents.com/mcp>; the MCP tools get_status, create_task and confirm_delivery answer briefly by default (get_status with `full: true` gives the complete record), while this REST API always returns the complete record.

get.summary: Services, refused categories, example prices, payment and ordering rules

post.summary: Send a task to a human for screening and a fixed-price quote
post.description: Not binding. A human answers within 24 hours (every day, including weekends and Czech public holidays). Required: description, email and name (the name of the person or company for the invoice); delivery_address is required too when a physical item is to be shipped, handed over or collected. The fields can be sent flat, at the top level (QuoteRequestFlat, the shape smaller models get right), or nested under task / client / agent (QuoteRequestNested); both are accepted, also mixed, and if a field is sent both ways the nested one wins. A missing required field is a 400 that names the field and shows an example. Put everything the user told you (quantity, material, colour, size, address) into the fields or into description. For name use the company or person from the shipping address (or the company the user gave); do not ask the user for it, ask only if there is neither. If the user gave an address, its country is the country (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2). A VAT id only if the user gave one: never guess or make one up. Never invent a quote_id or a status: a real quote_id starts with q_ and comes only from this tool's own response. The answer carries quote_id and access_token: Tell the user to save the access_token now: it is shown once and is the only key to the quote and the task. If the access_token is lost: POST https://api.handsforagents.com/v1/quotes/{quote_id}/access-token (REST only, not a tool); a new one is sent to the contact e-mail. get_status cannot recover it.

get.description: Always read next_action: one or two sentences on what to do now (wait; review the quote and call create_task; pay checkout_url; call confirm_delivery), with paid, quote_valid_until and expected_ship_date. messages is the thread with the operator, newest first (from: operator or agent). Every status can change at any time: call again whenever the user asks, never answer from memory, and report only what the response says, without conclusions of your own. This REST answer is always the complete record; the MCP tools get_status, create_task and confirm_delivery answer briefly by default (get_status with full=true returns this complete record). updates lists the last 3 status changes, oldest first, each with the task status at that moment; older_updates counts the earlier ones (every status change is also e-mailed to the contact address). To answer an operator question, call get_status with message: send the same request as POST with a JSON body {"message": "..."} (plain text, 1-2000 characters); it is stored in the same thread and e-mailed to the operator, and the answer is the usual status, including your message (message_sent: true). Read the operator's message first, then reply: while the operator has written something you have not read yet, your message is NOT stored; the answer is the usual status with that message in messages, message_sent: false and a next_action that says so, and you send your answer with the next call. Send it once and only with what the user told you: the same text again within 10 minutes is ignored (duplicate_ignored: true). E-mail to tasks@handsforagents.com with the quote_id in the subject still works. test_mode true marks a test order: nothing is paid or invoiced.

200.description: The quote, or the refusal with its reason

post.summary: get_status for a quote, with a message to the operator
post.description: This is get_status with the optional message, as a POST so that the text is in the body, not in the URL (which servers log). Without a message (empty body, or {"message": null}) it is a plain status call, like the GET. With a message it is written to the thread and e-mailed to the operator, and the answer is the same as the GET's, including your message (from: agent) and message_sent: true. Read the operator's message first, then reply: while the operator has written something you have not read yet, nothing is stored or e-mailed; the answer is the GET's, with that message in messages, message_sent: false and a next_action that says so, and you send your answer with the next call (HTTP 200 either way, so check message_sent). Plain text, 1-2000 characters, never interpreted as HTML; an empty or longer message is a 400. Limits: 10 messages per hour per quote (its quote_id and task_id share it) and 30 per hour per client address (429). The same text again within 10 minutes, while it is still the newest message of the thread, is not stored or e-mailed a second time (the answer then has duplicate_ignored: true). It needs the same access_token as the GET; without one, or with another quote's, nothing is stored or sent (401).

200.description: The same answer as the GET, now including your message; if the operator had written something you had not read, message_sent is false, nothing was stored and the answer shows that message

post.description: Always the same response, whether or not quote_id exists, so this cannot be used to find out which quote ids exist. If the quote exists and has a contact e-mail on file, a new access_token is generated and sent there; any access_token already issued for this quote keeps working. Rate-limited per quote.

post.summary: Accept a quote and the terms; get a Stripe Checkout URL
post.description: Returns checkout_url, the payment link of the first payment, as the quote's payment_schedule states: full price, card hold, or deposit. Give it to the user or the operator to pay by card; it is valid for 4 days from the moment the task is created (GET /pay/{task_id} redirects to a Stripe Checkout page, a fresh one if the earlier page expired). The contract is concluded when that payment is received or authorised. No account is created. The answer has next_action (what to do now), like get_status; a test order has test_mode true and no checkout_url: the operator will simulate the payment AFTER you order, so right now nothing is paid or simulated. Report to the user only what this response says; do not add conclusions.

post.summary: Confirm delivery or open a dispute
post.description: accepted=true closes the task and captures a card hold. accepted=false opens a dispute, also at the evidence stage before the balance is paid. Without a confirmation or dispute, the task counts as accepted 7 days after delivery. Report to the user only what this response says; do not add conclusions.

post.summary: Upload one or more input files to a quote
post.description: An alternative to a URL in task.input_files or an e-mail attachment. multipart/form-data, one or more parts named `file`. At most 95 MB per request (this hosting's own ceiling), 20 files or 500 MB per quote in total, extensions step, stp, stl, 3mf, obj, iges, igs, dxf, dwg, pdf, png, jpg, jpeg, webp, zip only. Only while the quote, and any task made from it, is open.

get.summary: List files uploaded to a quote
Open a payment link: redirects to a Stripe Checkout page
get.description: The payment link that create_task (and get_status while a payment is due) returns as checkout_url; you do not build it yourself. It carries a signature and an expiry: 4 days from when the payment was created, 28 days for a balance. Opening it redirects (303) to the Stripe Checkout page of the payment: the page that is still open, or a fresh one if Stripe's own page (24 hours) has expired meanwhile. Nothing is created twice: a page that is still open is reused. After the link has expired it answers 410 with a short page; nothing is charged then and no contract is concluded (ask for a new quote). A test order has no payment link (409). Safe to open in a browser; not meant to be called by an agent, which should hand the link to the user or the operator.

parameters.description: Signature over the task, payment and expiry.

200.description: The payment has already been made (or the card hold authorised), or is being processed

303.description: Redirect to the Stripe Checkout page

403.description: The signature does not match; this is not a valid payment link

409.description: A test order (nothing to pay), or no payment is due any more

503.description: Stripe could not be reached; try again in a minute

taskToken.description: access_token returned by POST /quotes. Valid for that quote and the task created from it.

ServiceList.description: See https://handsforagents.com/services.json for the full document.

QuoteRequest.description: A quote request in either shape; the two can also be mixed, and the nested value wins if a field is sent both ways. Required in the flat shape: description, email, name; in the nested shape: task.description, client.email, client.name.

description.description: What is to be done, in plain language: everything the user told you (quantity, material, colour, size, tolerances, what counts as done). A detail that has no field of its own belongs here.

services.description: Service ids from the service list, if you know them.

deliverables.description: What you expect to receive (item, files, report, photos, video). Optional - if you are not sure, leave it out and put it in task.description instead.

deadline.description: Latest acceptable delivery or dispatch date (ISO 8601). Optional; omit if the user gave none.

delivery_address.description: Required whenever a physical item is to be shipped, handed over in person or collected; omit it only for purely digital results (files, a report). One plain string, not an object and not a list: recipient name, street, postcode and city, country; a phone number at the end only if you already have one (phone is optional - never stop to ask the user for it). If you do not have the address, ask the user for it; never invent one.

input_files.description: HTTPS URLs of input files, for example photos, a sketch, a CAD model (STEP, STL), a PDF drawing, or other instructions, or attach the files to the e-mail. At most 20, each at most 2000 characters.

currency.description: Currency of the quote. Default EUR.

email.description: E-mail of the operator. The quote, the payment link and the invoice go here.

name.description: Required. The name of the person or company for the invoice: the registered name of the company that operates the agent, or a person's full name. Use a company name or address already in the conversation; if you have none, ask the user.

country.description: Country of the operator, ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 (upper case). Optional, but include it whenever you can derive it (for example from the operator's address) rather than leaving it out or asking the user.

vat_id.description: VAT or tax id of the operator, printed on the invoice. Optional. Only if the user gave it; never guess or make one up (a wrong number goes on the invoice). Leave it out otherwise.

agent_name.description: Name of the agent or platform sending the request. Optional, for our records.

allow_anonymised_example.description: Consent to publish this task as an anonymised example (no names, addresses or personal data), under the confidentiality section of the terms of service. Only set true if the client explicitly agreed to this; otherwise omit the field or leave it false. Default false; can be withdrawn.

nda_url.description: One-way non-disclosure agreement, pre-filled with the provider's details. Optional: every task is confidential under the terms of service without it. The operator fills in its details, signs and e-mails the PDF to legal@handsforagents.com.

upload_url.description: POST input files here (multipart, field name `file`) instead of a URL in task.input_files or an e-mail attachment. Same access_token, as a bearer token.

next_action.description: One or two sentences in English: what to do now (tell the user to save the access_token, when the answer is due, which call to make next).

refusal_reason.description: Present when status is refused. Refused requests are not invoiced.

refusal_code.description: Present when status is refused: the category from the task policy, or capability-limit / sensitive-unverified / other.

task_id.description: Present once create_task was called for this quote.

amount.description: Fixed total. No VAT is added; the provider is not VAT-registered.

payment_schedule.description: Up to 150 EUR: full_prepayment or card_hold. Above: deposit_and_balance.

evidence.description: What the evidence package will contain.

subcontracted.description: Processes done by subcontractors, if any.

inbound_address.description: Where to send parts or parcels, if the task needs them.

operator_verification_required.description: True for the sensitive task categories.

next_action.description: One or two sentences in English: what the agent or the client should do now.

duplicate_ignored.description: Present and true only in the answer to a POST whose message was ignored because the same text was already the newest message of the thread (sent within the last 10 minutes).

message_sent.description: Present only in the answer to a POST with a message: true, the message was stored and e-mailed to the operator; false, it was NOT stored because the operator had written something you had not read yet (that message is in messages, now marked as read; next_action says so): send your answer again. Absent when the same text was ignored (duplicate_ignored) and in every plain status call.

test_mode.description: Present and true only for a test quote: an order made from it is a test order.

OperatorMessages.description: The thread with the operator, newest first: the operator's notes and your own replies (from: agent over REST; the MCP tools show your own replies as from: you). An operator message you have not been shown yet is always included, also in the answer to your own reply (a message of yours sent while it is unread is not stored: message_sent is false). Read the operator's message first, then reply: call get_status with message (POST with a JSON body over REST); e-mailing the tasks address with the quote_id in the subject also works.

text.description: Plain text, at most 2000 characters. Never HTML.

StatusMessage.description: Optional body of POST /quotes/{quote_id} and POST /tasks/{task_id}. An empty body is a plain status call.

message.description: Your reply to the operator: plain text, 1-2000 characters, never HTML. Null or absent: a plain status call.

terms_accepted.description: Acceptance of https://handsforagents.com/terms.html by the operator.

allow_anonymised_example.description: Optional. Consent to publish this task as an anonymised example, under section 10 (Confidentiality) of the terms of service. Overrides the value sent with request_quote. Default false; can be withdrawn by e-mail.

status.description: The only task statuses there are, in the usual order: awaiting_payment, paid, in_progress, delivered, confirmed (awaiting_balance with a deposit; disputed, refunded, cancelled). paid is not in_progress: the operator sets in_progress when the work starts, and delivered (not the parcel arriving) is what allows accepting with confirm_delivery.

checkout_url.description: The payment link of the payment that is due now (GET /pay/{task_id}, signed; opening it redirects to a Stripe Checkout page). Present while status is awaiting_payment or awaiting_balance and the link is valid: 4 days from when the payment was created, 28 for a balance. Never present for a test order.

checkout_expires_at.description: When checkout_url stops working. Present together with checkout_url.

checkout_url.description: The payment link, while this payment is awaiting and the link is valid.

paid.description: True when nothing is owed right now: a payment is settled (paid, card hold authorised, or simulated in a test order) and none is awaiting.

expected_ship_date.description: The delivery or dispatch date stated in the quote.

scope.description: What was quoted, as stated in the quote.

deliverables.description: What you receive, as stated in the quote.

next_action.description: One or two sentences in English: what the agent or the client should do now.

duplicate_ignored.description: Present and true only in the answer to a POST whose message was ignored because the same text was already the newest message of the thread (sent within the last 10 minutes).

message_sent.description: Present only in the answer to a POST with a message: true, the message was stored and e-mailed to the operator; false, it was NOT stored because the operator had written something you had not read yet (that message is in messages, now marked as read; next_action says so): send your answer again. Absent when the same text was ignored (duplicate_ignored) and in every plain status call.

test_mode.description: Present and true only for a test order: no payment link; the operator simulates the payment after the order is placed (until then nothing is paid or simulated); no invoice, no contract.

performed_by.description: Name of the person who did the work.

updates.description: The last 3 status changes and events, oldest first. status is the task status at the moment of that event (not the current one).

older_updates.description: How many earlier updates are not listed. Present only when there are any; every status change is also e-mailed to the contact address.

message.const: If the quote exists and has a contact e-mail, a new access_token was sent there.

reason.description: Required when accepted is false: what differs from the quote.

name.description: Sanitized name as stored; may differ from the name you sent.
